primitives.name: Spatial Discrimination via Motion
primitives.verbatim_quote: 175 Enough has now been said to show that in the education of spatial discrimination the motions of impressions across sen-Bory surfaces must have been the principal agent in breaking p our consciousness of the surfaces into a consciousness of their parts.
primitives.assumptions: Consciousness of surfaces is initially unified; motion across sensory surfaces is the primary driver of spatial differentiation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when motion ceases, reverting to static perceptual states.

layer2.mapping: Maps sensory surface exploration to sequential state transitions in GSE, and to dynamic feature extraction in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Measurable changes in perceptual resolution during active exploration vs. passive observation.

primitives.name: Peripheral Sentinel Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: Even to-day the main function of the peripheral regions of our retina is that of sentinels, which, hen beams of light move over them, cry'Who goes there?' nd call the fovea to the spot.
primitives.assumptions: Peripheral vision acts as an alert system, triggering central focus when movement occurs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when the foveal fixation becomes too rigid, losing sensitivity to peripheral stimuli.

layer2.mapping: Maps sentinel activation to conformal prediction boundaries in GSI, and to reactive state-transitions in GSE.
layer2.telemetry: Response latency of foveal shift after peripheral stimulus detection.

primitives.name: Equivalence of Relative Motion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Of course movement of surface under object is (for purposes of stimulation) equivalent to movement of object over surface.
primitives.assumptions: The physical mechanism of stimulation depends only on relative displacement between object and surface.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when inertial frames cannot be distinguished, leading to perceptual ambiguity.

layer2.mapping: Maps relative motion equivalence to Galilean invariance principles in GSE, and to covariant feature learning in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Consistency of perceptual outcomes regardless of whether object or surface is moved.

primitives.name: Contrast Enhancement via Successive Contrast
primitives.verbatim_quote: If we make each single feeling of contrast = 1 (a supposition lar wo famrable to the state of rest), the sum of contrasts in the case of motion will be 8, against 1 in the state of rest.
primitives.assumptions: Successive contrasts created by motion compound linearly, amplifying perceived differences.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapses when temporal integration windows exceed critical values, causing motion blur.

layer2.mapping: Maps contrast enhancement to temporal differencing filters in GSI, and to predictive state updates in GSE.
layer2.telemetry: Increase in signal-to-noise ratio of visual features due to motion-induced temporal gradients.

Failure occurs when motion cues are absent or corrupted, leading to reduced discriminative power.
